messages.author: bc11fbb928eb77ff
messages.subject: exchanges between chains in Nimble?
parts:
Dear all,

I was wondering if the architecture of Nimble could allow exhanges of information or states between chains?

And if chains could be put at different temperatures?

What inspires my question is the parallel tempring literature that seems very useful in case of multiple local equilibria.

e.g.:
Miasojedow, B., Moulines, E. and Vihola, M. 2013. An adaptive parallel tempering algorithm. - Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 22: 649-664.

As I understand Nimble (as a user and not as a programmer), this is not possible, but I am not sure of this.

If possible, I could help implement these kinds of algorithms.

Sincerely,

Frédéric Gosselin

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: exchanges between chains in Nimble?
parts:
Hi Frédéric

I already have nimble code for the adaptive parallel tempering algorithm of Miasojedow (adapted from NImble's block sampler as it was this time last year).

It was a good challenge getting that sampler working, it took me about 10 days to get it working for a toy problem in population dynamics.  I had to copy and adapt the buildMCMC function so that it could accommodate the temperature ladder. I also had to define a virtual nimble function called sampler_APT that replaced the standard sampler_BASE. The sampler worked very nicely for the problem we were tackling, although the adaptive part proved to be not as fool proof as some of Vihola's other adaptive schemes (so I also added some monitors to track what that was doing).

If you'd like to try the code drop me an email at david.pleydell[AT]inra.fr.

Best
David

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: exchanges between chains in Nimble?
parts:
Thanks for the question, Frédéric.  It's great to hear how you did it, David.

It sounds like you took a reasonable path.  Some other ideas could include:

- Making a transformation of the model when it is defined so that all log probabilities are adjusted by the temperature.  I think this would involve making the temperature a part of the model itself.

- Making modified versions of sampler nimbleFunctions that could still inherit from sampler_BASE but could be told what the temperature node is via a control parameter.

- Making different sampler objects to be used at different temperatures so that any adaptive parameters adapt to the posterior at that particular temperature (an alternative would be to modify proposal scales based on the temperature).

Those are not all mutually exclusive.  Please keep us up to date on how it goes and whether any of these ideas are of interest.

-Perry

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: exchanges between chains in Nimble?
parts:
What did we do in NIMBLE 0.6-6 that broke your code?

Chris

Thanks Chris

It turned out that there were just two small issues.

First, the handling of defaults within each sampler. In past versions, we had things like this in the setup code of each sampler 
        adaptive       <- control$adaptive
        adaptScaleOnly <- control$adaptScaleOnly
        adaptInterval  <- control$adaptInterval
        scale          <- control$scale
        propCov        <- control$propCov
and now we need things like 
        logScale      <- if(!is.null(control$log))           control$log           else FALSE
        reflective    <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))    control$reflective    else FALSE
        adaptive      <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))      control$adaptive      else TRUE
        adaptInterval <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval)) control$adaptInterval else 200
        scale         <- if(!is.null(control$scale))         control$scale         else 1

Second, the way the limits are handled in the reflective sampler. We used to have this
        if(reflective) { 
            while(propValue < range[1] | propValue > range[2]) {
                if(propValue < range[1]) propValue <- 2*range[1] - propValue
                if(propValue > range[2]) propValue <- 2*range[2] - propValue
            } 
        } 
and now we need this
        if(reflective) { 
            lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
            upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
            while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
                if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
                if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
            }
        } 

With those fixes in place the code works fine on 0.6-6

parts: With those fixes in place the code works fine on 0.6-6

That said, I have hit much harder issues trying to turn this collection of scripts into an R package.  My main motivation was just to improve/standardise the documentation. But I have hit a tricky (for me) NAMESPACE / searchpath issue.

The code works fine when the functions have been called using source, but buildAPT fails if the functions have only been attached with library(NimbleSnippets)

The error message is 
Error in getClass(Class, where = topenv(parent.frame())) : 
  “nfRefClass_R_GlobalEnv45” is not a defined class

and it is generated inside the setup code of buildAPT at the line 
samplerFunctions[[ist]] <- conf$samplerConfs[[ss]]$buildSampler(model=model, mvSaved=mvSaved) 

The code for this fledgling R package is here https://github.com/DRJP/nimble-snippets/tree/buggyNamespace
And a script demonstrating the bug (and a hack with source) is here https://github.com/DRJP/nimble-snippets/blob/buggyNamespace/demo/APT_demo_DEBUG.R

I am building and installing (on Linux) with 
R CMD build nimble-snippets
R CMD INSTALL NimbleSnippets_1.0.1.tar.gz  ~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/

What is confusing is that no matter whether the source hack has been applied or not, I always have the following
parent.env(environment(buildAPT))
<environment: namespace:nimble>
so I am failling to see what is different in the searchpath between runs with and without calling the code with source.

Any pointers (excuse the pun) in the right direction would be very welcome.
David

messages.subject: Re: exchanges between chains in Nimble?
parts:
Hi David,

sorry about the delay in getting back to you on this. I just played around with your package and if you change

where = getLoadingNamespace()

to

where = getNamespace("NimbleSnippets")

for buildAPT() and your 4 samplers, your demo should run using the installed NimbleSnippets package.

Basically, getLoadingNamespace() is not set up such that it can handle the situation of samplers being defined in a package separate from NIMBLE. Now that we have your test case, we'll see about modifying this to handle things gracefully, but in the interim, the above change should do the trick.

chris

Many thanks Chris for this valuable insight. Indeed this does work nicely. Great!!!

There is however one small caveat. With this change in place I can no longer use roxygenize() to generate a NAMESPACE et al for an R package because roxygenize() returns the following error message 
    Error in assignClassDef(Class, classDef, where) : 
      class “nfRefClass_NimbleSnippets43” has a locked definition in package ‘NimbleSnippets’

As a work around I can...
1) switch to the original "where" statements
2) run roxygenize()
3) switch back to the correct "where" statements
4) Run R CMD build, check and INSTALL
This works and I have a couple of emacs macros to speed up switching the "where" statements.

Version v1.0.1 of NimbleSnippets is now available here. It is now compatible with Nimble 0.6-6. Anyone downloading the source can now use it to build an R package.

Best
David
